summary: Remove near-zero importance features (importance <= 1.0) to improve model signal clarity
rationale: Diagnostics reveal 19 features with importance <= 5.0 adding noise to the model. This iteration removes 6 base features with near-zero importance (<= 1.0): has_ever_won, long_layoff_over_1yr, fights_in_last_year, age_x_recent_vs_career_decline, underdog_specialization_advantage, and orthodox_vs_southpaw. By removing these low-value features, we reduce model noise and improve signal clarity, which should enhance edge detection for top 25% predictions. The change is conservative (removing only features with importance 1.0 or less) to avoid harming ensemble performance while targeting the primary goal of improving top_25_pct accuracy.
expected_effect: Expected to improve top_25_pct performance by reducing noise from low-importance features. The cleaner feature space should enable better edge detection and more confident predictions. Removing these 6 base features (which generate ~18 columns including f1_*, f2_*, *_diff variants) reduces model complexity without removing any high-importance predictive signals.
